Open the Workflow Runs group picker and select grouping by Workflow version.
Observe multiple v1 options without visible parent-workflow context. Search a parent workflow name and observe no match; search v1 and observe the ambiguous options.
Control: group by Workflow instead and search the parent name to identify it.

bugs.name: Local named TypeScript types remove Code-step configurable inputs without warning
bugs.summary: Using a same-file named type or interface for Code handler parameters removes configurable fields and saves an empty input, while equivalent inline annotations restore them.
bugs.expected: Equivalent supported same-file parameter type declarations should expose equivalent configurable inputs, or the editor should explain unsupported schema inference.
bugs.actual: Replacing inline input annotations with a local alias or interface removes the input fields without warning and retains empty input configuration after reload. Replacing the declaration with an equivalent inline annotation restores the fields.
reproSteps: Create a fresh saved workflow with a Code action and a main handler whose inline parameter type has fields such as userName, amount and active. Confirm those configuration inputs appear.
Move that same parameter shape into a local same-file type alias or interface and annotate the main parameter with the named type.
Save and observe that configurable inputs disappear without explanation and empty input configuration persists after reload.
Control: restore the equivalent inline parameter annotation and observe the expected input fields return.

bugs.name: Workflow variable step search hides existing steps when the query contains uppercase letters
bugs.summary: The workflow variable picker returns no available steps for uppercase queries that match existing step names.
bugs.expected: Searching for an existing step by its displayed name should find it regardless of query capitalization.
bugs.actual: Pick, PICK and Pick Record return No variables available while lowercase pick and empty search find Pick Record. Create and Launch also fail. Browsing without search maps the output successfully.
reproSteps: Create a manual workflow with Pick Record and a downstream action accepting a variable; allow saving to complete.
Open the downstream input’s variable picker and search for Pick, PICK or Pick Record. Observe no available variables.
Clear the query or enter lowercase pick. Observe the available step and map its output.
Compare uppercase field-level search inside a selected step, which works.

bugs.name: Mobile expanded workflow Code editor Back link does not close fullscreen
bugs.summary: The expanded Code editor remains fullscreen after its mobile Back link is clicked.
bugs.expected: Back to Code - Logic Function should close the expanded editor and return to the action panel.
bugs.actual: At 390px and 768px the Back link leaves the expanded editor open, covering Code and Test controls. At 769px and desktop the visible X closes it. Escape can recover.
reproSteps: Create a fresh manual workflow with a Code - Logic Function action and open it at mobile width.
Expand the code editor, then click Back to Code - Logic Function. Observe fullscreen remains open.
Compare tablet width 768px, then 769px or desktop where the X works; compare Escape recovery.

bugs.name: Fullscreen workflow Code input choices open behind the editor overlay
bugs.summary: Generated Boolean and enum input choices in the fullscreen workflow Code editor are hidden beneath its overlay and cannot be selected.
bugs.expected: Editable Code input selectors should display their choices above the fullscreen editor and allow selection, as the same inputs do in the ordinary side panel.
bugs.actual: Clicking a generated Boolean or enum selector mounts its choices behind the fullscreen overlay. The choices remain invisible and option-area clicks hit the overlay. Leaving fullscreen permits selection; returning shows the chosen value but still conceals the options.
reproSteps: Create a manual workflow with a Code - Logic Function action whose function parameters include a Boolean, such as enabled: boolean. Allow its input schema to appear.
Expand the Code editor to fullscreen and click the generated Boolean input. Observe no visible True/False choices and inability to select them.
Leave fullscreen and select True in the same input in the ordinary action panel. Return to fullscreen and observe True displayed, while reopening its choices remains unusable.
Compare the adjacent variable picker, which opens above the fullscreen editor. A generated string-enum selector also reproduces.

bugs.name: Typing a negative fractional Code input loses its sign and saves a positive value
bugs.summary: Sequential typing of a Code parameter between -1 and 0 converts its intermediate -0 to 0, saving the completed number with the wrong sign.
bugs.expected: Supported negative Code parameters should retain their sign during ordinary typing and save the same value as whole-value entry.
bugs.actual: Typing -0.25 with ordinary pauses displays positive 0.25, which remains saved after reload. Top-level and nested parameters reproduce. Negative values at or below -1, positive fractions and whole-value negative-fraction entry work.
reproSteps: Create a manual workflow with a Code action whose parameters include an unrestricted number, and wait for its generated input.
In the empty generated input, type -, 0, ., 2, 5 one key at a time with ordinary pauses. Observe the minus disappear at the intermediate -0.
Wait for saving, reload and reopen the action. Observe the saved positive 0.25. Repeat with a fresh workflow; a nested numeric parameter also reproduces.
Compare ordinary entry of -1.25 and 0.25 and whole-value entry of -0.25, which preserve the intended values.

bugs.name: Fractional scheduled hour overwrites a valid saved schedule with an invalid cron value
bugs.summary: The scheduled trigger hour accepts and saves 1.5 despite promising an integer; the invalid value persists after reload and prevents the schedule preview from operating.
bugs.expected: The UTC hour should enforce its stated integer range before replacing a valid saved schedule.
bugs.actual: Entering 1.5 in one edit saves hour 1.5, clears the integer-range field error and replaces the schedule and upcoming-execution preview with Invalid characters, got value: 1.5. Both the fraction and parser error survive reload. A whole-hour edit restores the preview.
reproSteps: Create a fresh scheduled workflow using a daily trigger and a valid saved UTC hour.
Replace the hour with 1.5 in one input event, such as pasting it. A keyboard-only variation types 15, moves the caret between the digits and inserts a decimal point.
Allow saving, then reload and reopen the trigger. Observe hour 1.5 and the cron parser error instead of a working schedule preview.
Repeat on a fresh workflow. Change the hour to a whole number such as 2 and verify the valid preview and saved value recover.

bugs.name: Changing a database trigger object conceals retained monitored fields and prevents runs
bugs.summary: Changing a Record is updated trigger from Companies to People retains Company-only monitored fields while showing an empty Fields selector, silently preventing later People updates from starting the workflow.
bugs.expected: The optional monitored-fields selector should accurately display its saved restrictions after an object change, or clear incompatible restrictions before activation. A visibly unrestricted trigger should behave like the working no-field-restriction control.
bugs.actual: After selecting Companies Annual Revenue and switching to People, the Fields selector shows its empty placeholder after reload, but saved settings retain annualRevenue. Activation succeeds, and saved Person name changes produce no new run. Clearing the retained restriction restores execution. A truly unrestricted People trigger looks the same and runs normally.
reproSteps: Create a disposable workflow with Record is updated, Companies, monitored field Annual Revenue, and a harmless Search Records action.
Change Record Type to People without editing Fields, wait for saving and reload. Observe the empty Select specific fields to listen to placeholder.
Activate and edit a fresh Person’s name. Observe no new workflow run, despite the seemingly unrestricted trigger.
As a control, configure a fresh People trigger without selected fields and verify the same name edits start it.
For recovery, switch the affected trigger back to Companies, uncheck the retained field, return to People and activate. Verify a later name edit starts a run.

bugs.name: Changing Workflow Runs grouping silently restores saved filters over pending edits
bugs.summary: Choosing Group by in a saved Workflow Runs view replaces its active unsaved filters with saved filters, silently changing which runs are shown.
bugs.expected: Changing grouping in the same view should retain its valid active filters and pending changes, or warn before discarding them.
bugs.actual: Removing a saved Failed status chip shows three mixed-status runs and Reset/Update view. Selecting Workflow run status grouping restores the Failed chip, hides pending-change controls and leaves only the failed run. Unsaved added filters are also discarded. Saving the filter edit before grouping preserves results.
reproSteps: Create harmless workflow runs with Failed, Completed and Stopped statuses and a disposable Workflow Runs Table view.
Save a Name filter isolating those runs together with Workflow run status = Failed.
Remove only the Failed chip without saving. Confirm all three runs and Reset/Update view are visible.
Choose Options > Group > Workflow run status. Observe the Failed filter return, the count drop to one and pending-change controls disappear.
Compare saving the filter removal before grouping, and opening/dismissing Options without selecting grouping; these preserve the intended mixed-status results.

bugs.name: Duplicating a workflow action selects the copy but its header renames the original
bugs.summary: After Duplicate node, the selected copy and side-panel body differ from the header’s target. Renaming from that header persistently changes the unselected original action.
bugs.expected: The selected action, editable side-panel header and configuration body should identify the same step after duplication, as they do after an ordinary node click.
bugs.actual: Duplicating Pick Record outlines Pick Record (Duplicate), but the panel header still identifies Pick Record. Entering a replacement title renames the original and leaves the selected copy unchanged, including after reload. The configuration body instead edits the copy. Explicitly clicking a node synchronizes the targets and restores correct renaming.
reproSteps: Create a fresh manual workflow with a Pick Record action and open that action in its editable side panel.
Choose Options > Duplicate node. Observe the copy’s selected outline and the panel header still naming the original.
Rename the action through the header and press Enter. Observe the unselected original acquire that name while the selected copy retains its duplicate name.
Reload and confirm the wrong-node rename persisted. Explicitly click the copy and rename it as a control; the copy now changes correctly.
A Delay action also reproduces. Its numeric configuration body follows the copy even while the header still renames the original.

bugs.name: A rejecting Filter stalls a trigger-adjacent Iterator without a successful external parent
bugs.summary: A finite Iterator placed directly after a manual trigger stops advancing when a loop Filter rejects an item, leaving its completed continuation unstarted and the saved run Running.
bugs.expected: A supported Filter inside a finite Iterator should stop only the current branch and let the Iterator advance or complete.
bugs.actual: With items alpha and beta, a Filter allowing alpha passes the first iteration and rejects the second. The loop-back Delay becomes Skipped, the Iterator remains Running and its completed-path Delay stays Not started after reload and waits exceeding a minute. Rejecting the first item also prevents later items from being processed. All-items-pass and successful-predecessor controls complete.
reproSteps: Create a fresh manual workflow with Iterator directly after the trigger and literal items alpha and beta.

Wire a loop containing a one-second Delay, a Filter Current Item Is alpha, then another one-second Delay returning to the Iterator. Add a one-second Delay on the Iterator completed path. Wait for configuration to save.
Test the workflow. Inspect both Filter iterations: alpha matches and beta does not. Observe the loop-back Delay skipped, Iterator Running and completed Delay Not started.
After more than 60 seconds, reload the run and confirm its stored state still has not advanced. Repeat with a fresh workflow.

Controls: allow both items through the Filter and observe completion. With the rejecting Filter retained, insert a successful one-second Delay before the Iterator; that external successful parent also restores completion.

bugs.name: Completed-branch Delay Input shows the Iterator first iteration instead of its completed context
bugs.summary: After a two-item Iterator finishes, its completed-branch Delay Input tab shows the first iteration values even though execution used the final completed Iterator result.
bugs.expected: A completed step’s Input inspector should represent the execution context passed to that step, consistently with the documented run-debugging behavior.
bugs.actual: A correctly committed Current Item Index Delay executes with final index 2 and the run completes, but its Input tab shows currentItem alpha, currentItemIndex 0 and hasProcessedAllItems false. The final stored Iterator result is index 2/true.
reproSteps: Create a manual workflow with an Iterator over two known items, alpha and beta, and a valid one-second Delay on its loop path.
On the Iterator completed branch, add a Delay whose Seconds uses Current Item Index. Explicitly commit the variable selection and verify the saved configuration.
Test the workflow and confirm successful completion with final Iterator result currentItemIndex 2 and hasProcessedAllItems true.
Inspect the completed-branch Delay’s Input tab and expand Iterator. Observe alpha, index 0 and false, including the consumed index highlighted as 0.
Compare the successful execution and stored final Iterator result; do not count an uncommitted variable or zero-duration execution failure as this display defect.

bugs.name: Workflow Form submits a previous valid date while displaying an incomplete replacement
bugs.summary: Editing a previously valid Form Date to an impossible or incomplete date leaves that new text visible, but Submit silently stores the previous valid date as the answer.
bugs.expected: Submitting a Form should represent the displayed response, or visibly reject or revert an incomplete edit before submitting a different value.
bugs.actual: After entering 11/12/2026, replacing it with 02/30/2026 leaves 02/30/202_ visible without an error. Dismissing the calendar and clicking Submit completes the run with the stale 2026-11-12 response, which remains after reload.
reproSteps: Create a manual workflow with a Form containing one Date input. Test the saved workflow.
Enter a valid date such as 11/12/2026 and click the Form title to close the calendar.
Replace the date with 02/30/2026. Observe the incomplete 02/30/202_ text and no explanatory validation message.
Click outside to close the calendar, then click Submit. Inspect the completed Form Output and persisted run state; the prior valid 2026-11-12 is submitted.

Control: replace the original date with a valid new date and verify that new answer submits. An invalid date entered into an initially empty optional field should be distinguished from this stale-previous-answer claim.

bugs.name: Group by None does not clear Workflow Runs relation grouping even after reload
bugs.summary: Choosing None in a Workflow Runs Table grouped by Workflow version or Workflow leaves the saved relation grouping intact across reload.
bugs.expected: The supported Group by None action should remove the selected grouping, including when a relation grouping currently has no configured groups.
bugs.actual: None closes the menu but Workflow version or Workflow remains selected. The saved view retains that grouping field and reload does not clear it. Switching first to Workflow run status and then None successfully clears grouping after reload.
reproSteps: Create a fresh Workflow Runs Table view and choose Group by Workflow version. Leave its relation groups unconfigured.
Choose Group by None, reopen Options and observe the previous grouping still selected.
Reload the same view and verify the relation grouping remains selected.
Repeat on a fresh view or with Workflow relation grouping.
Control: switch to Workflow run status grouping, then None. Confirm the saved grouping clears after reload, distinguishing a persistent no-op from the separate transient stale-page problem.

bugs.name: Workflow Run Flow diagrams stay clipped after navigation or viewport size changes
bugs.summary: The full Workflow Run Flow page keeps an obsolete horizontal diagram position after a tablet navigation drawer is collapsed or a 768px run page narrows to 390px, clipping step labels and completion marks.
bugs.expected: The run diagram should remain readable when its visible container size changes, as it does when loaded directly at the same final width.
bugs.actual: Opening a completed run behind expanded tablet navigation and collapsing it leaves both nodes partly beyond the left edge. Separately, resizing a correctly displayed 768px full run page to 390px leaves nodes beyond the right edge. The run remains completed; reload with navigation closed or normal canvas panning restores readability.
reproSteps: Create a manual workflow with a Search Records step and complete a run. Open its preview at 768px with navigation expanded, then Open the full run page.
Collapse navigation and inspect Flow. The left portions of the trigger and action labels are clipped. Control: load the same run at 768px with navigation already collapsed; labels fit.
Independent variant: load a completed full run Flow page at 768px with readable nodes, then narrow the viewport to 390px without reloading.
Observe nodes extend beyond the right canvas edge, clipping labels and success marks. Opening and closing the command menu after this resize does not restore readability.
Reload at 390px with navigation closed, or pan the canvas. The complete nodes and marks become readable. Repeat using fresh runs/workflows.

bugs.name: A valid Number answer bypasses another workflow Form field’s validation
bugs.summary: Entering a valid answer in one Number field re-enables workflow Form submission while another field still displays invalid text and its validation error.
bugs.expected: Submit should remain disabled while any Number answer has a validation error. Correcting another field must not clear the invalid field’s submission gate.
bugs.actual: With two uniquely named Number fields, entering abc in the first disables Submit. Entering 42 in the second re-enables Submit while abc and Invalid number remain. Submission completes with only the second answer. If the first previously held a valid number, submission instead retains that previous value behind the invalid replacement text.
reproSteps: Create and activate a saved manual workflow with a Form containing two Number fields with distinct labels, such as Alpha and Beta.
Start a fresh run and enter abc in Alpha. Confirm Invalid number is displayed and Submit is disabled.
Enter 42 in Beta without correcting Alpha. Observe Submit becomes usable while Alpha still shows abc and its error.
Submit and inspect the completed Form result: Beta is 42 and Alpha is omitted. Repeat in another fresh run.
Stale-answer variation: enter a valid Alpha value first, replace it with invalid text, then enter a valid Beta value and submit. The completed result retains the prior valid Alpha value.
Control: correct Alpha to a valid number and submit both valid answers; both appear correctly in the completed result.

bugs.name: HTTP body property content-type receives header validation and is omitted on save
bugs.summary: A newly entered content-type property in an HTTP Request Key/Value body is incorrectly treated as a reserved header and omitted from saved body configuration.
bugs.expected: Body property names should be validated as payload properties, independently of restrictions on manually entered HTTP headers.
bugs.actual: Entering content-type=document under Body Input > Key/Value shows “This key should be set through body input.” After reload the property is absent, while an ordinary body property remains. Raw JSON preserves a content-type property.
reproSteps: Create a fresh manual workflow and add an HTTP Request action using POST.
Set Body Input to Key/Value. Enter an ordinary property such as title=document and allow saving.
Add a body property content-type=document. Observe the red header-oriented validation message beneath its name.
Wait, reload and reopen the action. Observe that the ordinary property remains but content-type is absent.
Repeat on another fresh workflow. Control: a Raw JSON body containing a content-type property survives save and reload.

bugs.name: Deleting another HTTP header saves and locks a rejected Content-Type header
bugs.summary: Deleting an unrelated header saves a manually entered Content-Type header that normal editing rejects, then reload turns it into a disabled managed row.
bugs.expected: Deleting another row must preserve the same reserved-header validation as ordinary editing and must not save a rejected header as an uneditable managed value.
bugs.actual: A GET action rejects Content-Type=text/plain with “This key should be set through body input.” Deleting X-Temporary causes Content-Type to persist. After reload the warning disappears and its key, value and trash button are disabled. Without the deletion, only X-Temporary persists.
reproSteps: Create a fresh manual workflow and add an HTTP Request action using GET.
In Headers Input enter Content-Type=text/plain and observe the reserved-header validation warning.
Add X-Temporary=remove, wait normally, then delete only the X-Temporary row using its trash button.
Wait, reload and reopen the action. Observe that Content-Type=text/plain remains, its warning is gone and its key/value/delete controls are disabled.
Repeat with a fresh workflow. Control: reload the same rejected Content-Type plus ordinary X-Temporary setup without deleting a row; Content-Type is omitted and X-Temporary remains editable.

bugs.name: Workflow Update Record ignores a saved clear of Company revenue amount
bugs.summary: Clearing Annual Revenue Amount Micros saves a blank mapping, but a successful Update Record action retains the Company’s previous amount while applying the new currency.
bugs.expected: A selected amount explicitly cleared to null must clear the stored amount when Update Record executes.
bugs.actual: A Create Record action creates a Company with amountMicros 3210000/USD. Update Record configured with blank Amount Micros and EUR remains blank after reload, but execution returns 3210000/EUR and leaves that amount on the Company. Explicit 0/EUR correctly stores 0/EUR.
reproSteps: Create a manual workflow with Create Record for Companies, setting a unique name and Annual Revenue amountMicros 3210000/USD.
Add Update Record targeting the Company created by the first action and select Annual Revenue. Set Amount Micros to 0 and Currency Code to EUR. Wait for saving and test; confirm 0/EUR.
Clear only Amount Micros with Backspace or Delete, blur, wait for saving and reload. Reopen Update Record and confirm the amount is blank while EUR remains.
Test the saved workflow and inspect Update Record output and the created Company. The run succeeds but retains 3210000 while changing currency to EUR.
Repeat with a fresh workflow or a new duplicate whose record reference is explicitly remapped. Compare the passing explicit-zero control.

bugs.name: Workflow Update Record ignores saved No Status and retains the Task’s previous status
bugs.summary: Update Record saves No Status correctly, but successful execution leaves the Task’s existing status unchanged.
bugs.expected: Selecting Status under Fields to update and explicitly choosing No Status must clear the Task status when the saved action executes.
bugs.actual: After No Status saves and survives reload, the workflow completes successfully but Update Record returns TODO or IN_PROGRESS inherited from Create Record. Selecting Done instead updates the status correctly.
reproSteps: Create a manual workflow with Create Record for Tasks, a unique title and To do status.
Add Update Record targeting the created Task. Select Status under Fields to update, choose Done, wait for saving and test; confirm the run completes and output status is DONE.
Choose No Status in Update Record, wait for saving and reload. Reopen the action and confirm No Status remains selected.
Test the saved workflow. The run completes, but Update Record output and the Task retain TODO.
Repeat with a fresh Task starting In progress and with only Status selected for update; the successful action retains IN_PROGRESS. Compare the passing Done control.

bugs.name: Workflow Form date Clear leaves partial input visible when the answer was initially empty
bugs.summary: Clear closes the date picker but retains incomplete date text in an initially empty workflow Form input.
bugs.expected: The explicit Clear command should empty the displayed date input, including partial input.
bugs.actual: After entering an invalid or partial date in an initially empty Form Date field, clicking Clear closes the calendar but leaves text such as 02/30/202_ or 12/__/____ visible. Clearing a valid date empties the mask. Submitting the partial-input case still produces a null answer.
reproSteps: Create a manual workflow with a Form containing a Date field and test it with the date initially empty.
Enter 02/30/2026 so the masked input displays 02/30/202_. Open the calendar and click Clear.
Observe the calendar closes while the partial date remains visible. Repeat with partial input 12.
As a control, enter a valid date and click Clear; the input returns to its empty mask.

bugs.name: Reconnecting a workflow edge onto an existing action opens unwanted action creation
bugs.summary: An existing edge reconnect saves correctly but also opens Select Action and overlays its destination with a temporary Add an Action node.
bugs.expected: Reconnecting an edge onto an existing node should update that connection without starting node creation.
bugs.actual: Dragging the arrow end of an existing connection onto an existing action saves the reconnect, but Select Action opens and a temporary Add an Action placeholder and edge cover the destination. Closing the panel or reloading restores the correct saved graph. A new connection onto an existing node does not open action creation.
reproSteps: Create a manual workflow with two existing actions and a connection to the first action.
Select the existing connection and drag its arrow end onto the second existing action.
Observe the reconnect succeeds while Select Action opens and a temporary Add an Action placeholder appears over the destination.
Close the panel or reload; the unwanted placeholder disappears and the intended connection remains. Compare a new connection between existing nodes, which opens no creation panel.

bugs.name: Rejected Workflow Run status drag leaves the card in the destination column
bugs.summary: A forbidden Workflow Run status change is rejected by the server, but Kanban retains the optimistic column placement until reload.
bugs.expected: After a rejected status drag, the run card should return to its saved status column.
bugs.actual: Dragging a Failed workflow run into Completed displays a permission error, but the card remains under Completed. Its badge can disagree with the column or retain the optimistic label. Reload returns the card to Failed; the stored status was not changed.
reproSteps: Create a manual workflow that produces two Failed runs. Open Workflow Runs in a Kanban view grouped by run status.
Drag one owned Failed run into Completed and wait for the permission error.
Observe the card remains in Completed after the rejection and a settled wait. Repeat with the second failed run.
Reload and confirm both return to Failed. Compare an allowed Opportunity stage drag, which saves and remains in its destination after reload.

bugs.name: Reselecting a workflow condition field clears its saved comparison while displaying the old value
bugs.summary: Reselecting the current field can conceal an empty saved comparison and make a workflow Filter execute differently from its visible condition.
bugs.expected: The comparison shown in the editor should match the condition saved and executed after field reselection.
bugs.actual: After reselecting Workspace Member Id, the comparison input still shows the previous text or valid member ID, but the saved comparison is empty. Is can remain Is, leaving the panel visually unchanged. A Test then rejects the matching member and skips the downstream action. Reopening or reloading reveals the empty comparison.
reproSteps: Create a manual workflow with Filter: Workspace Member Id Is the current member ID, followed by a Create Record action. Save and Test to verify the Filter passes and the action executes.
Open the Filter field picker and explicitly reselect the current Workspace Member Id field. Observe the same Is condition and member ID remain visible.
Wait for the edit to save and Test again. The saved flow uses an empty comparison, the Filter returns false and the downstream action is skipped.
Reopen the Filter or reload to reveal the empty comparison. Re-enter the member ID and Test to restore the passing result; merely opening and dismissing the picker preserves it.

bugs.name: A stale schedule hour from valid typing is persisted by a later minute edit
bugs.summary: Typing a valid two-digit schedule hour can restore a stale prefix; editing only minutes then saves the wrong hour.
bugs.expected: A valid configured hour should remain consistent with the completed input, and editing minutes should preserve that hour.
bugs.actual: Fast entry of 23 can leave the hour field and preview at 2/02:00 even while a saved readback still holds 23. Changing only Minutes then saves hour 2 with the new minute. Reloading and reopening retains the wrong hour and preview.
reproSteps: Create a manual workflow, switch to a daily scheduled trigger, and configure an hour.
Replace the hour with 23 using fast ordinary typing; wait for saves. Repeat if needed until the field and preview show 2/02:00.
Change only Minutes, wait for the save, then reload and reopen the trigger. The hour remains 2 with the new minute.
Compare normal-speed entry, a one-digit hour edit, and retyping the intended hour; these controls preserve the intended setting.

bugs.name: Tab traps focus in Delay duration inputs and leaves edits unsaved
bugs.summary: Typing a Delay duration and pressing Tab leaves focus in the same input, so its blur-based save never runs and reload restores the old duration.
bugs.expected: Tab moves focus out of an editable Delay duration input and allows the editor to commit the new value.
bugs.actual: After changing Seconds from 0 to 5 and pressing Tab, the field keeps focus and displays 5 without saving. Reloading and reopening the action shows 0. Repeated Tab and a wait do not commit it. Clicking another field or leaving through normal in-app navigation does save the edit.
reproSteps: Create a disposable workflow with a Delay action using After a set amount of time and a known saved duration. A deactivated workflow can demonstrate the failure.
Change Seconds, press Tab and inspect the focused input. Wait before reloading.
Reload the workflow and reopen Delay; compare the old duration. Repeat on a fresh workflow.
As a control, change the duration and click another field before reloading; verify that edit persists.

bugs.name: Workflow Update Record ignores saved No record for a Person’s Company
bugs.summary: An Update Record action saves Company as No record but a successful run leaves the Person linked to the previous Company.
bugs.expected: A completed Update Record action applies its saved No record choice by clearing the selected Person’s Company relation.
bugs.actual: The saved action contains companyId:null with Company selected for update. The run and step report success, but the output and refreshed Person retain the old Company. Assigning a different Company works; another selected field can update in the same step while Company remains unchanged.
reproSteps: Create disposable Companies and People with existing Company links. Build a manual workflow with Update Record targeting one Person.
Select Company under Fields to update and choose No record in its picker. Close the editor, reload and confirm the saved choice.
Run the workflow and compare the Update Record result and refreshed Person’s Company with the requested clear.
Repeat for a fresh Person. Compare a non-null Company assignment and an ordinary record clear control.

bugs.name: Workflow Update Record ignores a saved Clear of Task Due Date
bugs.summary: The Due Date picker saves a null clear in Update Record, but successful execution leaves the Task’s previous date unchanged.
bugs.expected: A completed Update Record action applies its saved Due Date Clear by setting the selected Task’s dueAt to null.
bugs.actual: Due Date remains selected under Fields to update and the empty configuration remains on re-entry. The saved input contains dueAt:null. The workflow and update step complete successfully, but their output and the refreshed Task retain the old date. Setting a non-null date works.
reproSteps: Build a disposable workflow that creates a Task with a Due Date and then updates that Task using its returned ID.
Select Due Date under Update Record’s Fields to update, set a date and use the picker’s explicit Clear command. Close and reopen or reload to verify the saved empty configuration.
Run the workflow and compare Update Record’s output and the saved Task’s Due Date with the requested clear.
Repeat with a fresh Task. Compare an Update Record action assigning a different non-null Due Date.

bugs.name: Delay date picker is hidden beneath the mobile workflow panel
bugs.summary: The Delay date/time calendar opens beneath the mobile editor panel, preventing calendar selection while typed date entry still works.
bugs.expected: The Delay until date calendar opens visibly above the editor panel and accepts day selection on mobile and tablet.
bugs.actual: At tested 390px and 768px widths, focusing Delay until date mounts the calendar but its days are covered by the full-screen side panel. Clicking a covered day closes the picker without changing the date. Desktop selection and typed mobile date entry work.
reproSteps: Create a disposable manual workflow with a Delay action and select At a specific date or time.
At a 390px-wide viewport, open Delay until date and attempt to select a calendar day. Repeat with a fresh empty-date Delay and at tablet width.
Observe no visible calendar and no date change from the covered day click. Compare a wider desktop viewport and typing a date followed by reload.

bugs.name: Newly created draft is omitted from reopened versions history
bugs.summary: After Use as Draft creates a new saved draft, reopening workflow versions history can omit it while the versions count includes it.
bugs.expected: Workflow-filtered versions history should include the saved draft alongside the active and archived versions.
bugs.actual: On two fresh workflows, Use as Draft opens the saved v3 draft, but immediately reopening See Versions History shows only v2 Active and v1 Archived while the count is 3. A separate fresh workflow passes the same sequence.
reproSteps: Create an owned workflow, activate v1, create a draft from v1 and activate it as v2.
Open archived v1 and choose Use as Draft. Verify the new saved draft opens.
Immediately reopen See Versions History and inspect the filtered list and count.
Compare a separate fresh workflow and confirm its v3 Draft, v2 Active and v1 Archived all appear.

bugs.name: Update Record ignores a saved No currency selection
bugs.summary: A saved No currency choice is ignored when Update Record completes on an existing Company revenue currency.
bugs.expected: A successful Update Record should apply the saved null currency selection while retaining the separately configured amount.
bugs.actual: The historical run configuration shows No currency and amount 0, but successful Update Record output retains USD with amount 0 on repeated fresh Company runs. Changing only the currency choice to EUR returns 0/EUR. A nonzero null-currency update similarly retains the existing currency.
reproSteps: Create an owned manual workflow that creates a Company with USD annual revenue and then updates that Company.
In Update Record, select Annual Revenue, set amount 0 and choose No currency. Allow the configuration to save and reopen it.
Run the workflow and compare its saved Node configuration with successful Output: currency remains USD.
Repeat with fresh Company data; compare an explicit EUR assignment and a sibling Create Record with No currency.

bugs.name: Backspace does not persist deletion of an Iterator loop-start edge
bugs.summary: Backspace temporarily removes an Iterator loop-start connection, then the connection returns and remains after reload.
bugs.expected: A selectable and deletable loop-start connection should be removable through the canvas keyboard deletion path just as through its trash button.
bugs.actual: On two fresh workflows, the selected Iterator-to-Delay loop-start edge disappears briefly after Backspace, then returns gray and unselected. Reload retains it. The same edge deletes persistently through its trash button, and ordinary trigger/completed-branch edges delete persistently with Backspace.
reproSteps: Create an owned manual workflow containing an Iterator with a Delay in its loop.
Select the Iterator-to-Delay loop-start edge and press Backspace. Wait for the mutation response.
Observe the connection return, then reload and confirm it remains.
Compare the same edge trash button and Backspace on ordinary trigger and completed-branch connections; verify their deletions persist and nodes remain.

bugs.name: Open Delay Output stays empty after its run completes
bugs.summary: A Delay Output inspector opened while a test run is pending stays at Empty Object after successful completion; reopening reveals the saved result.
bugs.expected: An already-open run-step Output should reflect the completed step’s result, as the full run-page inspector does.
bugs.actual: On two fresh workflows, holding the test side-panel Delay Output open leaves Empty Object after the run has completed. Returning to Flow shows Completed; reopening the same Delay shows result.success true. Opening the pending Output from the full run page updates live without reopening.
reproSteps: Create a disposable owned manual workflow with a duration Delay, save it, and click Test.
While the Delay is pending, open its Output in the test side panel and leave it open beyond completion.
Observe Empty Object remains; return to Flow to see Completed, then reopen the same step to see result.success true.
Repeat with a separate workflow. As controls, first open Output after completion and hold pending Output open from the full run page; both show the successful result.

bugs.name: Canvas Add node ignores its first action selection
bugs.summary: Right-clicking the canvas, choosing Add node, then selecting Delay leaves Select Action instead of creating the node. A second selection works; plus/header insertion controls work.
bugs.expected: The documented right-click Add node flow should create the chosen action on its first selection.
bugs.actual: Right-clicking the canvas, choosing Add node, then selecting Delay leaves Select Action instead of creating the node. A second selection works; plus/header insertion controls work.
reproSteps: Create an owned manual workflow and right-click empty canvas.
Choose Add node, then select Delay once and wait. Observe Select Action remains without a new action.
Select the action again; creation succeeds. Compare plus/header insertion on fresh data.

bugs.name: Changing If/Else to Delay leaves saved empty branch placeholders
bugs.summary: After Delay is changed to If/Else, reloaded, and changed back to Delay, two generated EMPTY branch placeholders remain disconnected and survive reload. Direct If/Else deletion removes its placeholders.
bugs.expected: Replacing a branching action with a nonbranching action should clean up its generated empty branch placeholders consistently with deletion.
bugs.actual: After Delay is changed to If/Else, reloaded, and changed back to Delay, two generated EMPTY branch placeholders remain disconnected and survive reload. Direct If/Else deletion removes its placeholders.
reproSteps: Create an owned workflow with Delay and change it to If/Else.
Reload to verify its generated empty branch endpoints, then change it back to Delay.
Reload and observe the two detached Add an Action placeholders remain. Compare deleting a separate If/Else action.

bugs.name: Workflow run details omit the documented Duration
bugs.summary: Completed and stopped runs show start and end timestamps but no run-level Duration in their details.
bugs.expected: Run details should expose Duration as explicitly listed in the workflow runs guide.
bugs.actual: Completed and stopped runs show start and end timestamps but no run-level Duration in their details.
reproSteps: Create and execute an owned workflow; inspect a completed run with start and end timestamps.
Inspect separate stopped runs with saved start/end timestamps.
Observe that the run details do not display Duration.

bugs.name: Adding an action after converting an existing placeholder to Iterator crashes the workflow editor
bugs.summary: After converting an existing Else or Iterator-child placeholder to Iterator, subsequent Filter or Create Record insertion can replace the workflow editor with a recoverable page error.
bugs.expected: Adding an offered action after placeholder-to-Iterator conversion should keep the editor usable.
bugs.actual: After replacing an existing If/Else Else placeholder with Iterator, adding a disconnected Filter through header Add a Node replaces the workflow editor with Sorry, something went wrong / Please refresh the page. Two fresh workflows reproduce; reload retains the saved Filter and restores editable configuration. Connected Filter insertion through the converted Iterator loop connector also crashes before reload. Converting an outer Iterator child placeholder to a nested Iterator and choosing Create Record from its loop handle produces the same editor crash on two fresh workflows; reload recovers.
reproSteps: Create an owned manual workflow containing Code and If/Else.
Replace the existing Else branch placeholder with Iterator, preserving the live diagram without reload.
Use the header Add a Node action to add a disconnected Filter. Observe the main editor crash while the navigation sidebar remains.
Reload to recover and configure the saved Filter; compare connected branch Filter insertion and header insertion after reload.

Additional verified variation: After converting an Else placeholder to Iterator, insert Filter from the loop connector instead of the header. Create a manual workflow with an If/Else action. Configure a condition and change its Else placeholder action to Iterator. Set Iterator items to Alpha and Beta and leave the editor to save. Without reloading the workflow, drag the Iterator loop connector onto blank canvas and choose Filter. Observe the page-content error instead of Filter Conditions. Reload; the saved Filter can then be opened and edited. Compare a fresh Iterator created directly from Add Node: dragging its loop connector and choosing Filter opens Conditions successfully, including with saved Alpha and Beta items.

Additional verified variation: Convert an outer Iterator child placeholder into a nested Iterator, then insert Create Record from its loop handle. Create a manual workflow with an outer Iterator and two literal items. Select its existing Add an Action child placeholder and change its action type to Iterator. Drag from the inner Iterator’s loop handle to open Select Action, then choose Create Record. Observe the full-page error. Reload to recover. Compare a fresh nested Iterator created through the outer loop edge’s plus insertion control; adding its Create Record action keeps the editor usable.

bugs.name: Ctrl+Enter bypasses an invalid Number Form submission gate
bugs.summary: A workflow Form displays Invalid number and disables Submit, but clicking blank space in the Form panel and pressing Ctrl+Enter completes the run with an empty result. Two fresh runs reproduce on one saved workflow. A valid button submission returns its entered numbers.
bugs.expected: The Form shortcut should enforce the same explicit invalid-Number submission gate as the disabled Submit button.
bugs.actual: A workflow Form displays Invalid number and disables Submit, but clicking blank space in the Form panel and pressing Ctrl+Enter completes the run with an empty result. Two fresh runs reproduce on one saved workflow. A valid button submission returns its entered numbers.
reproSteps: Create and save a manual workflow with a Form containing Number fields labelled Amount and Quantity, then test it.
Enter abc in Amount and verify Invalid number with Submit disabled.
Click a blank area or heading of the Form panel to move focus out of the Number input, then press Ctrl+Enter.
Inspect Completed status and empty output, including after reload. Repeat with a fresh run; compare valid numbers submitted with the button.

bugs.name: Typing a negative fraction saves a positive Filter threshold
bugs.summary: Sequentially typing a negative fraction such as -0.4 into a numeric Filter threshold can display and save 0.4. Reopening after reload retains the positive value on two fresh workflows. A run using the incorrectly positive threshold evaluates differently from the corrected negative control.
bugs.expected: Ordinary entry of a supported signed threshold should preserve its numeric meaning when saved.
bugs.actual: Sequentially typing a negative fraction such as -0.4 into a numeric Filter threshold can display and save 0.4. Reopening after reload retains the positive value on two fresh workflows. A run using the incorrectly positive threshold evaluates differently from the corrected negative control.
reproSteps: Create an owned manual workflow with a Number Form answer and a Filter on that answer using Greater than or equal.
In the empty numeric threshold, type -0.4 sequentially, allowing the intermediate -0 value to render. Leave the field and let saving finish.
Reopen after reload and observe positive 0.4; repeat on a fresh workflow.
Compare complete-value negative replacement and a negative nonzero integer. Run with an answer between the intended negative and saved positive thresholds and compare the corrected negative control.

bugs.name: Workflow Create Record strips a significant leading zero from phone numbers
bugs.summary: In a People Create Record action, selecting Italy +39 and entering 0669812345 changes the phone input to 669812345. The altered digits persist after saving and reload on two fresh workflows. A completed test creates a Person containing +39 669812345.
bugs.expected: Phone entry should preserve significant national-number digits, including the Italian leading zero, while keeping the calling code separate.
bugs.actual: In a People Create Record action, selecting Italy +39 and entering 0669812345 changes the phone input to 669812345. The altered digits persist after saving and reload on two fresh workflows. A completed test creates a Person containing +39 669812345.
reproSteps: Create a manual workflow with a People Create Record action and unique own Person data.
Select Italy +39, enter 0669812345 into the initially empty Phone Number input, then leave the field and let saving finish.
Observe 669812345; reload, reopen the action, and observe the changed digits remain. Repeat on a fresh workflow.
Test the action and inspect the created Person phone value. Compare 3669812345, which remains unchanged through saving and reload.

bugs.name: Duplicating an If/Else node blocks its original matching branch
bugs.summary: Duplicating an individual If/Else creates a disconnected copy whose branches still point to the original child Filters. The original If/Else succeeds, but its matching Filter remains Not started while the run reports Completed. Two fresh workflows reproduce; deleting the duplicate restores branch execution. An activated configuration also reproduces.
bugs.expected: Duplicating an individual node should preserve execution of the original connected matching branch. A disconnected copy should not block that branch.
bugs.actual: Duplicating an individual If/Else creates a disconnected copy whose branches still point to the original child Filters. The original If/Else succeeds, but its matching Filter remains Not started while the run reports Completed. Two fresh workflows reproduce; deleting the duplicate restores branch execution. An activated configuration also reproduces.
reproSteps: Create an owned manual workflow with If/Else using Trigger Metadata Workspace Member Id Contains -, with one Filter on each branch. Configure the child Filters to accept that member ID and save. Run a control and verify the matching Filter executes.
In the original If/Else settings footer choose Duplicate node. Leave the new copy disconnected and allow saving to finish.
Test and open the full run. Observe Completed and a successful original If/Else result, but its matching Filter remains Not started. Reload the run to confirm its saved state.
Delete the disconnected copy and repeat Test: the matching Filter executes. Repeat duplication on a fresh workflow; the failure also occurs after activating the affected configuration.

bugs.name: Malformed scheduled-date input surfaces an internal serialization error
bugs.summary: A scheduled Delay mapped from a Text Form answer fails on not-a-date with ERR user_script:281: Cannot serialise number instead of an invalid-input validation diagnostic. The failure repeats and remains in the run output after reopening. A valid future date completes; missing and past dates produce input-specific validation errors.
bugs.expected: Malformed scheduled-date input should be rejected as invalid input with useful validation feedback, rather than surfacing the internal queue serialization exception.
bugs.actual: A scheduled Delay mapped from a Text Form answer fails on not-a-date with ERR user_script:281: Cannot serialise number instead of an invalid-input validation diagnostic. The failure repeats and remains in the run output after reopening. A valid future date completes; missing and past dates produce input-specific validation errors.
reproSteps: Create an owned manual workflow with a Text Form field named Delay target followed by Delay configured for a scheduled date mapped from that answer. Save the workflow.
Run Test, submit not-a-date, and inspect the failed Delay Output and Input. Observe the internal serialization error with delayTarget:not-a-date.
Repeat in a new run of the same workflow and reopen the first run; the error remains.
Compare a valid future ISO timestamp, which completes with success:true. A past timestamp and an empty value produce the existing past-date and required-date validation errors.

bugs.name: Long Form labels clip input settings controls in a narrow panel
bugs.summary: At 390px, a Text Form field labelled Mobile explanation for responsive testing expands its input settings beyond the right edge. The section close button disappears and Placeholder is partially clipped, while the top-level panel close remains visible. Two fresh workflows reproduce, including reopening after reload.
bugs.expected: Supported Label and Placeholder configuration controls should remain visible and usable within the available settings panel.
bugs.actual: At 390px, a Text Form field labelled Mobile explanation for responsive testing expands its input settings beyond the right edge. The section close button disappears and Placeholder is partially clipped, while the top-level panel close remains visible. Two fresh workflows reproduce, including reopening after reload.
reproSteps: Create an owned manual workflow with a Form action and a Text field. At 390×844 open its Input settings; the default short label shows the section close button and full Placeholder input.
Change Label to Mobile explanation for responsive testing, leave the field, close settings through the field preview, and reopen them.
Observe the section close button beyond the viewport and the clipped Placeholder input. Horizontal scrolling does not reveal them. Repeat after saving/reload on a fresh workflow.
Compare the short label at 390px and the long label at 768px, which fit. Clicking the field preview still closes settings, and the top-level panel close remains available.

bugs.name: Discarded workflow versions offer a Restore action that always fails
bugs.summary: After a saved v2 draft is discarded successfully, reopening its retained version page shows a deleted banner with Restore. Clicking Restore reports You do not have permission to perform this workflow action, and the version remains deleted after reload. Both fresh workflows reproduce; the header Restore command also fails after confirmation.
bugs.expected: The interface should hide unsupported standalone version restoration or provide a working supported action instead of offering Restore that unconditionally fails.
bugs.actual: After a saved v2 draft is discarded successfully, reopening its retained version page shows a deleted banner with Restore. Clicking Restore reports You do not have permission to perform this workflow action, and the version remains deleted after reload. Both fresh workflows reproduce; the header Restore command also fails after confirmation.
reproSteps: Create a manual workflow with a Code action and activate it. Create a new draft, add a second Code action, save it and retain its v2 version-page URL.
Reload the draft and confirm its two actions and Draft state without a deleted banner. Discard Draft from the parent workflow. Confirm the parent is Active again with one action.
Open the retained v2 version page and click Restore in the deleted-record banner. Observe the permission error and unchanged deleted state after reload.
On a fresh workflow repeat the sequence. Also try the header Restore command and confirm restoration; it fails with the same permission error.

bugs.name: Workflow Update Record ignores saved No record for Company Account Owner
bugs.summary: A saved Update Record action has Company Account Owner selected with No record, and its executed configuration retains accountOwnerId:null. The run completes successfully but returns the previous owner, which remains on the refreshed Company. Assigning Tim Apple or Jony Ive works; clearing Jony while updating Name changes the Name but retains Jony.
bugs.expected: Update Record should clear the Company Account Owner when the saved selected value is No record.
bugs.actual: A saved Update Record action has Company Account Owner selected with No record, and its executed configuration retains accountOwnerId:null. The run completes successfully but returns the previous owner, which remains on the refreshed Company. Assigning Tim Apple or Jony Ive works; clearing Jony while updating Name changes the Name but retains Jony.
reproSteps: Create an owned manual workflow with Create Record Companies followed by Update Record. Target the created Company, select Account Owner and assign Tim Apple; run and confirm the saved Company has Tim as owner.
Change Update Record to target that existing Company explicitly. Keep Account Owner selected, choose No record, let the configuration save, reload and verify No record remains selected.
Test again. Inspect Update Record output and refresh the original Company: the run succeeds but the previous Account Owner remains.

Assign Jony Ive through the same action and verify success. Choose No record again while changing Name, save/reload and run: Name updates while Jony remains. Repeat on another owned Company with a duplicated and remapped workflow.

bugs.name: Replacing a deleted Iterator loop action overlaps its controller card
bugs.summary: After deleting the sole loop action and inserting Create Record through the empty loop edge, the replacement overlaps the Iterator card. Both fresh workflows reproduce; the overlap remains after reopening and in a completed run diagram. The replacement remains configurable and the Notes test completes.
bugs.expected: Adding a supported replacement loop action should place its card separately from the Iterator so both remain readable.
bugs.actual: After deleting the sole loop action and inserting Create Record through the empty loop edge, the replacement overlaps the Iterator card. Both fresh workflows reproduce; the overlap remains after reopening and in a completed run diagram. The replacement remains configurable and the Notes test completes.
reproSteps: Create an owned manual workflow with Iterator items alpha and beta. Add Search Records inside its loop, using Notes with Limit 1 and Offset 0.
Delete Search Records. Use the plus control on the now-empty Iterator loop edge and select Create Record.

Observe Create Record overlapping the Iterator card. Reopen the workflow and confirm the placement remains. Configure Create Record for an owned Note and test; the completed run also displays overlapping cards.
Compare a fresh Iterator where Create Record is chosen from the initial Add an Action placeholder without deleting a loop action; the cards are positioned separately.

bugs.name: Workflow Test runs the saved numeric value while a rejected replacement remains displayed
bugs.summary: An invalid numeric replacement remains visible in Create Record while Test executes the earlier saved value, making the displayed draft misleading.
bugs.expected: The editor should make clear that rejected numeric text is unsaved and Test will execute the previous accepted value, or require resolving the draft before testing.
bugs.actual: The Create Record editor displays invalid numeric text and Invalid number. Test can still complete using saved null or the previous valid amount; it does not execute or save the invalid text.
reproSteps: Create a manual workflow with a Companies Create Record action, a unique Name and Annual Revenue currency USD.
Enter abc into Amount Micros and leave the invalid draft visible. Run Test.
Inspect the successful output: the Company is created with the previously saved amount, such as null.
Control: save a valid numeric amount, then replace its displayed text with 12oops. Test uses the valid saved amount while the invalid replacement remains displayed.

bugs.name: Valid five-minute cron preview shows an invalid-expression description and duplicate times
bugs.summary: A displayed valid five-field custom cron expression can coexist with an invalid-expression description and duplicate upcoming execution times.
bugs.expected: The custom expression */5 * * * * should describe every five minutes and show successive distinct upcoming times.
bugs.actual: The reported preview displayed */5 * * * * but described an invalid expression with Expected 4-6 fields, got 3 and showed duplicate upcoming times.
reproSteps: Create a workflow with a scheduled trigger and choose Custom cron.
Replace the expression with */5 * * * * and leave the field.
Inspect the schedule description and three upcoming execution times for the reported invalid-expression message and duplicates.

bugs.name: Use as Draft warns of an existing draft while opening the requested version
bugs.summary: After another tab activates a newer workflow version, Use as Draft on the older version can report an existing draft while Go to Draft opens the requested older settings.
bugs.expected: When no outstanding draft exists, using an archived version as a draft should create it without claiming a prior draft conflict.
bugs.actual: The original report observed A draft already exists after Use as Draft, then Go to Draft opened the requested three-second Delay and retained it after refresh.
reproSteps: Create a manual workflow with a three-second Delay and activate it. In tab A use See Active Version and leave that version open.
In tab B edit Delay to four then five seconds, commit the edits, activate and refresh to confirm Active with five seconds.
Return to tab A, where the older three-second version is now Archived, and click Use as Draft once.
Inspect the existing-draft warning. Choose Go to Draft without Override; inspect the three-second setting and refresh.

bugs.name: Typed number-array configuration saves nonnumeric text without validation
bugs.summary: A workflow Code input declared as a number array accepts and retains literal nonnumeric text as an array member without array-field validation.
bugs.expected: An input declared as an array of numbers should reject or identify nonnumeric literal members before treating the configuration as accepted.
bugs.actual: Entering abc through the typed number-array editor saves and reopens the literal string member without array-field validation, while invalid scalar numeric input reports Invalid number.
reproSteps: Create a workflow Code action with an input schema containing a number-array parameter and a scalar-number control.
Enter abc into the number-array editor using Enter or Add item. Allow the configuration to save.
Reopen or reload the configuration and observe the retained abc member without an array validation message.
As a control, enter abc into the scalar-number field and observe Invalid number.

bugs.name: Stored Company mapping appears empty in the Create Record editor
bugs.summary: The seeded Create Person editor shows the empty Select placeholder for a stored Company relation expression. Historical execution resolves companyId and correctly links the Person; freshly UI-authored nested relation mappings display normally.
bugs.expected: The Create Record editor should represent a stored supported Company mapping consistently with the mapping used by execution.
bugs.actual: The seeded Create Person editor shows the empty Select placeholder for a stored Company relation expression. Historical execution resolves companyId and correctly links the Person; freshly UI-authored nested relation mappings display normally.
reproSteps: Open the seeded Quick Lead workflow containing Create Company followed by Create Person.
Inspect the Create Person Company selector, which displays Select despite a saved companyId expression referencing Create Company.
Test through the rendered form and inspect the run’s input/output: the mapping executes and the Person links to the created Company.
Compare a freshly UI-authored Company mapping, which uses the current nested relation shape and remains visible after reload.

bugs.name: Editing two Delay duration fields quickly silently loses the second change
bugs.summary: Rapidly updating two numeric duration fields in a Delay action causes the second input to revert to its previously saved value. Waiting between edits allows each value to save.
bugs.expected: Both entered duration values should persist when moving normally between fields, without silently dropping the second change.
bugs.actual: Second field edits are overwritten by an earlier field's save/re-render. Reproduced twice with different values, confirmed in saved run input and after reopening the action. Editing the second field alone and waiting saves it correctly.
reproSteps: Create a disposable saved workflow with a Delay set to Minutes 0 and Seconds 3.
In one natural rapid edit sequence, change Minutes to 1, then Seconds to 0, then blur by clicking Days. Do not add artificial network delays.
Inspect the settled editor and saved run input; the historical failure retains Seconds 3 instead of 0.
Repeat with different valid values and reopen the action. Compare editing only the second field or waiting between edits. This is intermittent.

bugs.name: A duplicated workflow shows 'Created by: System' instead of the user who duplicated it
bugs.summary: A user-invoked duplicate displays Created by System while normal user-created workflows display the initiating member. Readback of the duplicate contains source MANUAL, name System and a null workspaceMemberId.
bugs.expected: A user-invoked workflow duplication should retain the initiating user’s creator attribution, consistently with normal user creation.
bugs.actual: A user-invoked duplicate displays Created by System while normal user-created workflows display the initiating member. Readback of the duplicate contains source MANUAL, name System and a null workspaceMemberId.
reproSteps: Create and save a uniquely named workflow as the signed-in workspace member. Confirm its Created by attribution names that member.
Use the workflow Command Menu to Duplicate Workflow.
Open the Workflows list and compare the source and duplicate creator values. Observe System on the duplicate.

bugs.name: Restoring and reactivating a workflow makes one event execute twice
bugs.summary: After deleting, restoring, and reactivating an active Record-created workflow, a single matching record creation launches two runs and duplicates action output.
bugs.expected: A single matching record-created event should start exactly one run after restore/reactivation.
bugs.actual: After a passing one-event/one-run baseline, deleting, restoring and reactivating the workflow makes one newly created matching Note start two completed runs. Both reference the same trigger record ID and create distinct output Notes.
reproSteps: Create and activate a Record-created workflow on Notes with a unique title filter and a Create Note action whose output title does not match that filter.
Use one harmless Create Record workflow action to create one matching Note; confirm one event-driven run and output as baseline.
Delete the event-driven workflow, restore it, reload, and reactivate it.
Create one more matching Note through the same producer workflow. Inspect two completed consumer runs sharing the same trigger record ID and producing distinct output Notes.

bugs.name: Update Record editor misleadingly displays an unsaved Stage=New value
bugs.summary: Selecting Stage under Fields to update displays New without storing a stage value in objectRecord. The saved action contains the edited Name only. Explicitly selecting New stores stage NEW correctly.
bugs.expected: The Update Record editor should distinguish an unset Stage from an explicitly configured New value.
bugs.actual: Selecting Stage under Fields to update displays New without storing a stage value in objectRecord. The saved action contains the edited Name only. Explicitly selecting New stores stage NEW correctly.
reproSteps: Create a workflow with an Opportunity Update Record action and select Stage and Name under Fields to update.
Leave the displayed Stage New untouched and enter a valid Name. Allow saving to complete.
Inspect the displayed Stage and saved action configuration. Stage appears New, but objectRecord contains the Name without a stage value.
Explicitly select New and compare the saved configuration, which now contains stage NEW.

bugs.name: Restored workflow run remains pending beyond Delay while healthy control completes
bugs.summary: After deletion during a pending Delay and restoration beyond its deadline, bounded observations show the original run still Running/Pending with its downstream action unstarted. A new run of the restored same-version configuration completes normally.
bugs.expected: Deletion/restoration should leave a run in a coherent waiting or terminal state rather than a pending state whose expired Delay no longer advances. This entry does not require automatic resumption as the only acceptable lifecycle policy.
bugs.actual: After deletion during a pending Delay and restoration beyond its deadline, bounded observations show the original run still Running/Pending with its downstream action unstarted. A new run of the restored same-version configuration completes normally.
reproSteps: Create a disposable manual workflow with Delay 15 seconds followed by a harmless Create Note action.
Test and delete the workflow while its Delay is pending. Leave it deleted beyond the configured deadline.
Restore the workflow, reopen the same run and reload. At bounded follow-up checks, observe Running/Pending with the downstream action unstarted.
Test the restored workflow without deleting it as a control and confirm the same Delay duration completes normally.

bugs.name: Opening a test run full page hides the left branch behind the details panel
bugs.summary: On two runs at 1440 by 1000, opening the full run page left its left branch completely behind the details panel and upstream nodes partly covered. Panning revealed the nodes.
bugs.expected: Opening a run full page should position its graph within the available canvas so both branches are visible.
bugs.actual: On two runs at 1440 by 1000, opening the full run page left its left branch completely behind the details panel and upstream nodes partly covered. Panning revealed the nodes.
reproSteps: Create a manual workflow with Form, If/Else and separate actions on both branches.
Test the workflow and submit the form at a desktop viewport such as 1440 by 1000.
Open the run from its side panel to its full page.
Observe the left branch hidden behind the details panel; pan the canvas to reveal the nodes.
